transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I came in today because... well, I just can't keep my mind on my actual experiments at work anymore. I work as a physical scientist, and lately, my focus is just completely gone. 

If I'm on an important grant call or sitting in a safety meeting, I'll get completely derailed by the smallest things. I'll notice a pump vibration in the lab, or hear a student's side comment, or even just remember some odd peak in an old data spectrum. Next thing I know, I'm off chasing that tiny detail for hours, while the actual project everyone needs from me just falls apart. It's becoming a really serious problem, and I need to figure out what's going on.
Has this difficulty focusing and getting distracted by small details always been something you've struggled with, or is this something new that's started more recently?

No, it's definitely a newer issue. I've always been pretty good at staying on track before this. It's really been going on for about seven months now... basically right around the time I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
Around the time this focus problem started seven months ago, did you notice any changes in your mood—like feeling more sad, empty, or down—or did you start feeling more anxious or worried?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I haven't felt sad or empty at all. And I wouldn't say I've been anxious or worried, either... just frustrated that I can't get my actual work done. But no, my mood hasn't been down.
Over these past seven months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like sleeping more or less than usual—or changes in your overall energy level?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely changed. Most nights I'm only getting maybe two or three hours... I'll often just fall asleep right on the couch with my laptop still open. 

But I don't feel tired at all. I wake up feeling completely sharp and ready to get right back to work. Honestly, lately it just feels like sleep is an inefficient interruption to everything I'm trying to do.

When you're working on these projects and feeling sharp despite the minimal sleep, do you feel like you have more energy and confidence than usual, or like you're able to accomplish more than you normally could?

Yes, absolutely. I definitely feel like I can accomplish a lot more right now. I mean, I'm at the lab before anyone else even arrives in the morning. 

I'll be in there rewriting protocols, rearranging the instrument schedules, emailing our collaborators in three different countries... and just starting all these new analyses at the exact same time. I just have so much energy for it. Honestly, sitting still right now just feels like I'm wasting the one chance I have to finally fix everything.
Over these past seven months, has this high-energy, sharp feeling and decreased need for sleep stayed pretty much the same the whole time, or has it come and gone in waves or cycles?

It's been pretty constant. This whole thing has been going on for about seven months straight. It basically started right when I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project at work, and it hasn't let up since.

During these seven months, have there been any periods—even brief ones—where your mood dipped lower, or where you felt less energetic and more pessimistic or unmotivated, before bouncing back to this high-energy state?

No, I haven't had any dips like that. I haven't felt down or unmotivated at all. It's... it's really just been this constant high gear the entire seven months. I honestly haven't had a single day where I felt pessimistic or lacked energy.

During these seven months, have you noticed your thoughts racing or moving very quickly from one idea to the next? Or have you had any beliefs about having special abilities or insights that seem different from how you'd normally think about yourself?

Well, my thoughts definitely move fast. There's just so much to do. And as for special abilities... I don't know if I'd call it special, but I just know I'm the only one who can fix this. I genuinely believe I can rescue the entire multi-site project by myself. I can redesign the whole spectroscopy approach, mentor every single student better than their actual advisors can, and still beat the grant deadline. It's all completely possible if people would just stop getting in my way and slowing me down.

When you say you're the only one who can fix the project and redesign the entire spectroscopy approach—have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?
No, I haven't. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there or anything like that. It's really just my own thoughts. I just see the solutions to the project very clearly, that's all.
